title: Transmission-Based Precautions & PPE: Suspected Tuberculosis (LVN Scope)
subtitle: 45 y/o male with a chronic productive cough, night sweats, and weight loss — the LVN must recognize the need for airborne precautions, use PPE correctly, and match precautions to the route
nursesNote: 1000 - 45 y/o male admitted with a 4-week productive cough now with blood-streaked sputum (hemoptysis), drenching night sweats, unintentional 10-pound weight loss, and low-grade fevers. He recently stayed in a congregate shelter and reports a known TB exposure. Active pulmonary tuberculosis is suspected; sputum for acid-fast bacilli (AFB) has been ordered. He needs placement and precautions. The LVN practices under the direction of the RN/provider.

patient.name: J. Okafor
patient.admitDate: Admitted today; suspected active pulmonary tuberculosis

steps.title: Recognize Cues
steps.inst: Select the THREE (3) findings that MOST suggest possible active pulmonary tuberculosis requiring airborne precautions.

opts.text: Productive cough for over 3 weeks with blood-streaked sputum (hemoptysis)
opts.rat: A prolonged productive cough with hemoptysis is a classic presentation of pulmonary TB.

opts.text: Drenching night sweats, unintentional weight loss, and low-grade fevers
opts.rat: Night sweats, weight loss, and low-grade fever are hallmark constitutional symptoms of TB.

opts.text: Recent congregate-shelter stay and a known TB exposure
opts.rat: Congregate living and a known exposure are significant risk factors for active TB.

opts.text: Blood pressure at his baseline
opts.rat: A baseline blood pressure is reassuring and not a TB cue.

opts.text: His pain is controlled
opts.rat: Controlled pain is unrelated to the infection-control concern.

opts.text: Skin over the sacrum is intact
opts.rat: Intact skin is a reassuring, unrelated finding.

opts.text: The peripheral IV site is without redness
opts.rat: A clean IV site is reassuring but not related to TB.

steps.title: Analyze Cues
steps.inst: Select the THREE (3) statements that correctly reflect infection-control reasoning.

opts.text: Possible active pulmonary TB spreads by the airborne route and requires airborne precautions: a negative-pressure (airborne infection isolation) room with the door closed and a fit-tested N95 respirator for anyone entering; the client wears a surgical mask if transported
opts.rat: TB requires airborne precautions with an N95 and a negative-pressure room; the client masks during transport.

opts.text: Standard precautions apply to all clients (hand hygiene, PPE for anticipated contact with blood/body fluids); transmission-based precautions are added based on the suspected organism and route
opts.rat: Standard precautions are universal; transmission-based precautions are layered on by route.

opts.text: Airborne precautions differ from droplet (surgical mask; e.g., influenza, pertussis) and contact (gown and gloves; e.g., MRSA, C. difficile) — matching the precaution to the route is essential
opts.rat: Correctly matching precautions to the transmission route protects clients and staff.

opts.text: A surgical mask is sufficient protection for staff entering the room of a client with suspected TB
opts.rat: A fit-tested N95 respirator (not a surgical mask) is required for airborne precautions.

opts.text: The client can be placed in any room with the door open
opts.rat: Airborne precautions require a negative-pressure room with the door kept closed.

opts.text: Precautions are unnecessary until the diagnosis is confirmed
opts.rat: Precautions are implemented based on suspicion, before confirmation, to prevent transmission.

steps.title: Prioritize
steps.inst: Drag the steps into the correct order to PUT ON (don) PPE before entering (1 = first).

opts.text: Perform hand hygiene
opts.rat: Hand hygiene is performed before donning PPE.

opts.text: Put on the gown
opts.rat: The gown is donned first among the PPE items.

opts.text: Put on the N95 respirator and perform a seal check
opts.rat: The respirator/mask goes on next, with a seal check for the N95.

opts.text: Put on goggles or a face shield
opts.rat: Eye protection is donned after the respirator.

opts.text: Put on gloves (over the gown cuffs)
opts.rat: Gloves go on last, pulled over the gown cuffs.

steps.title: Generate Solutions
steps.inst: Select the THREE (3) actions that are appropriate.

opts.text: Place the client in a negative-pressure airborne infection isolation room with the door closed and use a fit-tested N95 respirator when entering
opts.rat: Correct room and respiratory protection for airborne precautions.

opts.text: Apply standard precautions plus airborne precautions, and have the client wear a surgical mask during any necessary transport
opts.rat: Layering airborne precautions on standard precautions and masking the client for transport are correct.

opts.text: Teach the client cough etiquette (cover cough, use tissues, hand hygiene) and the reason for isolation, and ensure the AFB sputum specimen is collected as ordered
opts.rat: Source control, education, and timely diagnostic collection support safe, effective care.

opts.text: Use only a surgical mask in a regular room
opts.rat: This does not meet airborne precautions; an N95 and negative-pressure room are required.

opts.text: Discontinue precautions because the diagnosis is not yet confirmed
opts.rat: Precautions stay in place based on suspicion until TB is ruled out.

opts.text: Transport the client through the unit without a mask
opts.rat: The client must wear a surgical mask during transport to contain droplets/droplet nuclei.

steps.title: Take Action
steps.inst: Drag the steps into the correct order to REMOVE (doff) PPE when leaving (1 = first).

opts.text: Remove gloves
opts.rat: Gloves (the most contaminated) are removed first.

opts.text: Remove goggles or face shield
opts.rat: Eye protection is removed next, handling by the clean straps/arms.

opts.text: Remove the gown
opts.rat: The gown is removed, rolling it away from the body.

opts.text: Leave the room, then remove the N95 respirator outside the room
opts.rat: The respirator is removed AFTER exiting the airborne isolation room.

opts.text: Perform hand hygiene
opts.rat: Hand hygiene is performed after removing PPE (and between steps as needed).

steps.title: Apply & Evaluate
steps.sub: Match each condition to its precaution type
steps.inst: Classify each condition by the transmission-based precaution it primarily requires.

opts.text: Active pulmonary tuberculosis
opts.rat: TB spreads via airborne droplet nuclei — airborne precautions (N95, negative-pressure room).

opts.text: Measles (rubeola)
opts.rat: Measles is airborne — airborne precautions are required.

opts.text: Influenza
opts.rat: Influenza spreads by respiratory droplets — droplet precautions (surgical mask).

opts.text: Pertussis (whooping cough)
opts.rat: Pertussis is droplet-spread — droplet precautions.

opts.text: Meningococcal (bacterial) meningitis
opts.rat: Neisseria meningitidis spreads by droplets — droplet precautions.

opts.text: Clostridioides difficile (C. difficile)
opts.rat: C. difficile spreads by contact with spores — contact precautions, with soap-and-water handwashing (alcohol gel does not kill spores).

opts.text: MRSA wound infection
opts.rat: MRSA spreads by contact — contact precautions (gown and gloves).

opts.text: Scabies
opts.rat: Scabies spreads by direct skin contact — contact precautions.

reference: Aligned to the NCSBN NCLEX-PN Test Plan client-need category: Safety and Infection Control (standard/transmission-based precautions and PPE) using the NCSBN Clinical Judgment Measurement Model, and supporting an under-weighted LVN blueprint area (Safety and Infection Control is 10-16% of the NCLEX-PN exam). Concepts reflect standard nursing and CDC infection-control practice at LVN scope: standard precautions for all clients (hand hygiene, PPE for anticipated blood/body-fluid contact) plus transmission-based precautions layered by route; airborne precautions for tuberculosis, measles, and varicella (N95 respirator, negative-pressure airborne infection isolation room, door closed; client masks for transport); droplet precautions for influenza, pertussis, and meningococcal meningitis (surgical mask); and contact precautions for MRSA, C. difficile (with soap-and-water handwashing because alcohol gel does not kill spores), and scabies (gown and gloves). PPE donning order: hand hygiene, gown, mask/respirator, goggles/face shield, gloves; doffing order: gloves, goggles/face shield, gown, then exit and remove the respirator outside the room, followed by hand hygiene. Note: varicella and disseminated zoster require both airborne and contact precautions; this set uses single-route examples for the matching exercise. Apply within current CDC guidance, BVNPT regulations, and facility policy, which can change. Lab and vital-sign values use standard reference ranges and are illustrative for the scenario; exact clinical figures are confirmed on faculty review by Joseph Ongongo, LPT.
